jobs.occupation: Senior Developer to support the Green Energy Transition
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced software developer with a passion for building high-quality applications? Do you enjoy solving complex technical challenges and working closely with business experts to create solutions that support the efficient, reliable, and secure operation of the Nordic power grid? If you are looking to make an impact in supporting the green transition of the energy sector across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark, you might be the person we are looking for.  

Join a fast-developing Nordic company and become a part of an agile environment where we develop innovative solutions. Nordic RCC is an important contributor to the green energy transition, supporting the Nordic transmission system operators in ensuring efficient and secure operations of the Nordic electricity power system.  

As part of our continued growth, Application Development is expanding significantly. We are strengthening our department with five Senior Developers and two Lead Developers, creating exciting opportunities to join a growing team and help shape the future of software development at Nordic RCC. 

Your role   

As a Senior Developer in Application Development, you will join a collaborative team of approximately 23 developers. Together, you will design, develop, and maintain internal applications that support our current and future business services. Working closely with product owners, architects, engineers, operators, and UX specialists, you will help translate business needs into robust technical solutions. 

You will be part of an application team that values sustainable solutions over quick fixes. We actively collaborate across applications and business services to identify common solutions, increase quality, and continuously improve the way we work. 

What you will do:

• 
Design, develop, and maintain robust applications using C# and .NET. 

• 
Write clean, maintainable, testable, and well-documented code following established design patterns and development standards. 

• 
Transform complex engineering and operational requirements into effective software solutions by collaborating closely with architects, product owners, engineers, operators, and UX designers to build solutions that meet business and operational needs. 

• 
Contribute to technical improvements, modernization efforts, and continuous optimization of existing applications. 

• 
Participate in code reviews and help ensure high quality, reliability, and maintainability across solutions. 

• 
Support troubleshooting and resolution of production issues. 

• 
Serve as a technical role model within the team and mentor colleagues who are developing their technical skills. 

• 
Stay current with new technologies, tools, and development practices relevant to Nordic RCC's technology landscape. 

Technology Stack:

• 
Primary languages and frameworks  C#, .NET, SolidJS, JavaScript/TypeScript, Functional programming, Python  

• 
Architecture, design patterns & integrations  Clean Architecture, SOLID, Event-driven Architecture, Message-driven Architecture, REST APIs 

• 
Databases & Storage Relational databases (SQL Server), NoSQL databases (MongoDB), GridFS, S3 

• 
Infrastructure & Platform (on-prem)  Kubernetes (on-prem), Docker, Rancher, Prometheus/Grafana, ArgoCD, NginX  

• 
Tooling and collaboration  Git, Visual Studio, VS Code, JetBrains Rider, Azure DevOps, CI/CD pipelines 

We’re looking for someone with:  

• 
Collaborative Mindset: You work closely with Application Architects, Product Owners, and fellow developers, contributing technical expertise, mentoring colleagues, and helping to ensure maintainable, scalable, and robust solutions. 

• 
Technical Foundation: A degree in Computer Science, IT, Software Engineering, or a related field. 

• 
Relevant Expertise: Experience developing enterprise-grade applications in C#/.NET, with a solid understanding of software architecture, design patterns, and modern development practices. 

• 
Continuous Improvement: You identify opportunities to improve code quality, system reliability, team practices, and developer productivity. 

• 
Nice to have: Experience working with functional programming, Clean Architecture principles, Azure DevOps, Kubernetes and Scrum processes.  

• 
Energy Sector Knowledge: Familiarity with the power systems domain is a plus but not required.  

 If you do not tick all the boxes, but think you could be a good match, don’t hesitate to apply for this position.   

What We Offer: A Flexible and Inclusive Workplace  

You will join a diverse organization of 23 nationalities, where inclusivity is celebrated, with more than 30% women on board (and a commitment to improving this balance). We are located in Copenhagen Towers office in Ørestad, with the flexibility to balance on-site and remote work 2 days a week.  

At Nordic RCC, we live by the values of fellowship, curiosity, respect, and transparency—values defined by our employees that shape how we collaborate and innovate. If you see yourself thriving in such an environment, we’d love to hear from you.  

Note that as part of the recruitment process, the candidate must undergo a satisfactory background check. The position is also conditioned upon a national security clearance. Both will be facilitated by Nordic RCC. You can read more on security clearance here. Please also note that the process includes that any spouse, registered partner, cohabitant, steady partner, co-resident, child over 18 living at home and parent with the same address as the candidate must also consent to be examined.   

Application deadline and contact information  

Please apply online (in English) no later than 15/11-2026. Interviews will be held on a rolling basis up until the right candidate has been found.  

To ensure a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request that you do not include photographs in your CVs or application materials.  

A cover letter is not required, but we kindly ask you to include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are interested in the position. Applications are only accepted through our online recruitment system. 

If you have any questions, please contact Pernille Yde Juul Hansen, Manager, Application Development pyh@nordic-rcc.net / +45 3092 3111

jobs.occupation: Would you like to combine your engineering studies with practical experience in project management and learn how technical solutions and business priorities come together?
jobs.description:
Would you like to combine your engineering studies with practical experience in project management and learn how technical solutions and business priorities come together?

At Gram Equipment, we develop and deliver equipment for industrial ice cream production worldwide. We are looking for an engineering student to join our Project Management team in Kolding, either as an intern or a student worker.

You will work alongside experienced colleagues and gain insight into how we coordinate projects, from technical requirements and planning to delivery. Along the way, you will learn how mechanical solutions, customer expectations, budgets and deadlines influence project decisions.

What you will be doing
You will support our project managers in their daily work, with tasks adapted to your skills, interests and study requirements. Your tasks may include:

• Supporting project planning and following up on milestones, deadlines and outstanding actions.
• Preparing and updating project documentation, status reports and meeting materials.
• Participating in project meetings and following up on agreed actions.
• Helping coordinate activities across Engineering, Sales, Production, Installation and Service.
• Supporting the follow-up on project costs, changes and risks.
• Contributing ideas to improve project processes and ways of working.

As you develop your understanding of our projects, you will have the opportunity to take responsibility for defined tasks with guidance from the team.

Who we are looking for
You are studying Mechanical Engineering, Global Business Engineering or a related engineering programme. You have a good understanding of mechanical principles and an interest in the business side of engineering, particularly how technical decisions affect costs, delivery and customer value.

We also imagine that you:

• Are curious about project management and eager to apply your knowledge in practice.
• Work in a structured way and follow through on your tasks.
• Enjoy collaborating with people across different functions.
• Take initiative and ask questions when you need input.
• Communicate clearly in English, both spoken and written.
You do not need previous project management experience. What matters is your willingness to learn and contribute.

What we offer
You will gain practical experience in an international engineering company, with support and feedback from experienced project managers. You will work on real projects and develop your technical, commercial and coordination skills.

Our main office in Kolding offers an informal working environment with dedicated colleagues.

Looking for an internship? We will agree on the duration, scope and learning objectives in line with your study programme.

Looking for a student job? We will agree on working hours that fit in with your studies, with flexibility during exam periods.

Interested?

Please send your CV and a short application explaining your motivation. Let us know whether you are interested in an internship, a student job or either option, and include your preferred start date and availability.

We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.occupation: Sales Manager, German Market | Based in Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Are you fluent in German, based in Copenhagen, and ready to help ambitious restaurants grow? Join DinnerBooking and help us expand our presence in Germany. 

At DinnerBooking, we are building a booking system that brings restaurants and guests together, and we have a lot of fun along the way. With more than 20 million guest bookings annually and 1,400+ restaurants across 11 markets, we help restaurants reach their full business potential. 

We are looking for a proactive and commercially driven Sales Manager based in Copenhagen to grow our customer base in Germany. You will combine your German language skills and understanding of the market with a structured approach to outbound sales. 

Why join DinnerBooking? 

Besides building a fantastic product, we take pride in our culture. Your ideas matter, your opinions will be heard, and you will be part of a team that supports each other. 

We are problem solvers, colleagues, and friends who want each other to succeed, both professionally and personally. 

Your role 

You will be responsible for identifying and engaging restaurant customers in Germany. You will join an ambitious international sales team, share ideas and work together to turn opportunities into lasting customer relationships. 

Your responsibilities will include: 

• 
Identifying and contacting potential customers in the German restaurant market. 

• 
Starting conversations through outbound calls and emails and following up. 

• 
Conducting online meetings and product demonstrations in German. 

• 
Managing the sales process from first contact to signed agreement. 

• 
Maintaining a structured and updated pipeline in our CRM system. 

• 
Working closely with colleagues to ensure a smooth handover and onboarding for new customers. 

What you bring 

• 
You are based in Copenhagen. 

• 
Fluency in German and a good command of English, both spoken and written. 

• 
1 to 3 years of outbound sales experience. 

• 
Confidence in opening doors, starting conversations, and building relationships. 

• 
A structured approach to managing your pipeline and following up on opportunities. 

• 
A proactive mindset and the ability to stay motivated and take ownership of your results. 

• 
An empathetic and energetic personality, with a genuine interest in people and their businesses. 

Nice to have, but not required 

• 
Experience in the restaurant or hospitality industry. 

• 
Experience selling SaaS or other B2B solutions. 

• 
A track record of strong sales results. 

• 
Experience with HubSpot or a similar CRM system. 

• 
An understanding of the German restaurant market. 

What you can expect from us 

• 
Responsibility for sales in Germany. 

• 
An international team with strong commercial experience. 

• 
Training in our product, sales approach, and the needs of our restaurant customers. 

• 
The opportunity to make a direct impact on our growth in Germany. 

• 
A supportive working environment with room for ideas and professional development. 

• 
A compensation package with a component based on performance. 

Interested? 

Send your application and CV in English. We would love to hear about your sales experience, your connection to the German market, and why you would like to join DinnerBooking.

jobs.occupation: Two-year Postdoc position on Spintronic Quantum-inspired Computing
jobs.description:
Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a 2-year Postdoctoral Researcher position within the newly funded QUANTRONIC – Spintronic Pseudo-Qubits for Room-Temperature Quantum Computing project, supported by the Villum Experiment programme of Villum Fonden.

We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to investigate a new class of spintronic pseudo-qubits (p-qubits) based on spin-orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions (SOT-MTJs). The project explores whether engineered stochastic spintronic devices can reproduce key computational mechanisms associated with quantum systems - including superposition-like states, probability-amplitude-based interference, and entanglement-like correlations—without relying on fragile quantum coherence or cryogenic operation.

QUANTRONIC is a high-risk, high-gain research project positioned at the intersection of spintronics, probabilistic computing, quantum-inspired computing, nanoelectronics, and integrated circuit design. The central concept is a novel SOT-MTJ architecture designed to represent and manipulate probability amplitudes and to enable synchronization between multiple pseudo-qubits. The project will combine physics-based modelling, device design and fabrication, experimental characterization, and system-level demonstrations.

The successful candidate will work within SDU Microelectronics and collaborate closely with international partners, particularly INL – International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory, on the design and fabrication of spintronic devices.

The position is expected to start in February 2027, with the specific starting date to be agreed with the successful candidate.

 

As a Postdoctoral Researcher in QUANTRONIC, your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Develop and refine physics-based compact models of SOT-MTJ-based pseudo-qubits, including stochastic switching and inter-device coupling.

• 
Develop Verilog-A models and integrate them into circuit-level simulation environments such as Cadence.

• 
Investigate the physical requirements for controlling probabilistic states and representing probability amplitudes in spintronic devices.

• 
Collaborate with project partners on the design and fabrication of SOT-MTJ devices and arrays.

• 
Experimentally characterize standalone devices and coupled arrays, including stochastic switching, synchronization, and entanglement-like correlations.

• 
Investigate quantum-inspired gate operations and system-level demonstrations using networks of pseudo-qubits.

• 
Contribute to proof-of-concept demonstrations, including integer factorization and other quantum-inspired computational problems.

• 
Publish research results in high-quality international journals and conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results.

• 
Collaborate with researchers in spintronics, probabilistic computing, microelectronics, materials science, and quantum information.

 

What we offer

• 
A unique opportunity to work on a high-risk, high-gain research concept exploring a new computational regime between classical probabilistic and quantum computing.

• 
A stimulating research environment within SDU Microelectronics, a growing research section with expertise in spintronics, probabilistic computing, neuromorphic computing, analog/digital IC design, and emerging computing architectures.

• 
Access to advanced facilities for electronic design, device characterization, measurement, and system prototyping.

• 
Close collaboration with INL – International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory on spintronic device technology and fabrication.

• 
Opportunities to collaborate with national and international researchers in spintronics, quantum-inspired computing, quantum technologies, and nanoelectronics.

• 
An open, international, and collaborative research environment within SDU's Faculty of Engineering, supporting interdisciplinary research across electronics, physics, materials science, and computing.

• 
Strong opportunities for developing an independent research profile in an emerging area of probabilistic and quantum-inspired hardware.

 

What we expect

Applicants should hold a PhD in electronic engineering, electrical engineering, applied physics, nanotechnology, spintronics, or a closely related field.

The ideal candidate should have experience in one or more of the following areas:

• 
Spintronics and magnetic devices, particularly MTJs, STT-MTJs, SOT-MTJs, or related technologies.

• 
Physics-based modelling of nanoscale or magnetic devices.

• 
Verilog-A, SPICE, and Cadence or comparable circuit/device simulation environments.

• 
Experimental characterization of electronic, magnetic, or spintronic devices.

• 
Stochastic or probabilistic computing systems.

Experience in micromagnetic simulation, magnetotransport measurements, nanofabrication, probabilistic computing, or quantum/quantum-inspired computing will be considered a strong advantage.

We are particularly interested in candidates who are enthusiastic about working across traditional disciplinary boundaries and are comfortable combining device physics, modelling, experimentation, and computing concepts.

The successful candidate should be able to work independently while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary and international research team. Excellent written and spoken English and strong communication skills are required.

 

Workplace description 

The successful candidate will join SDU Microelectronics, a dynamic and expanding section at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME). The section conducts internationally recognized research in integrated circuits, spintronics, photonics, and neuromorphic computing, and plays a central role in SDU’s ambition to be a national and European hub for semiconductor and chip innovation. 

 

Further information 

For further information about the position, please contact Professor Farshad Moradi (moradi@sdu.dk / email), Head of the SDU Microelectronics section and Associate Professor Hooman Farkhani (farkhani@sdu.dk / email), Deputy Head of SDU Microelectronics. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Summary and documentation of experience in teaching, if relevant to the position. 

• 
A research statement may be included.

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 10, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is February 2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

jobs.occupation: Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions
jobs.description:
Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions  Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences University of Copenhagen  The University seeks to appoint a tenure track assistant professor to commence 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.   Information on the department can be found at: http://www.sund.ku.dk/.   Subject area: Infectious disease epidemiology, modelling, animal health, One Health, and sustainable health systems  The Tenure-Track Assistant Professor will lead research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, with particular emphasis on how changes in environmental conditions, animal populations, production systems, and management practices influence disease emergence, transmission, and control. The position will combine infectious disease epidemiology, mathematical and statistical modelling, data science, and economic analysis to generate evidence supporting disease preparedness, prevention, and control.  The successful candidate will:   	
• Lead independent research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, including the influence of environmental and production system changes. 	
• Develop and apply simulation, epidemiological, and statistical models to assess disease and spillover risks, evaluate mitigation and control strategies, and quantify their economic implications. 	
• Demonstrate strong programming skills in R and other relevant programming languages, including experience in managing, processing, and analysing large and complex datasets. 	
• Have experience in developing and applying epidemiological disease-spread models, including model calibration, validation, parameter estimation, and calculation of epidemiological indicators such as the basic reproduction number (R₀) across different animal species and production systems. 	
• Design and implement epidemiological modelling frameworks. 	
• Validate and calibrate models using large-scale national datasets, ensuring scientific robustness, methodological validity, and relevance for policy and decision-making. 	
• Translate research findings into evidence supporting risk-based disease prevention, preparedness, and control.  	
• Establish and maintain collaborations with key stakeholders, including the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration, industry partners such as SEGES and Landbrug & Fødevarer (L&F), and international organisations such as the FAO. 	
• Lead and secure independent research funding through competitive national and international funding calls. The position requires demonstrated experience in securing external funding, as well as the ambition to develop research ideas into externally funded projects and provide scientific leadership for such projects within the TIPTON Research Group. 	
• Contribute to the development and delivery of One Health and sustainability teaching, with a particular focus on infectious diseases, disease preparedness, and the interactions between animal, human, and environmental health. 	
• Contribute to teaching in data science, including data management, dataset preparation and handling, statistical analysis, programming, and the analysis of large-scale and complex datasets. 	
• Supervise students and contribute to research capacity building within infectious disease epidemiology, disease modelling, data science, and One Health. 	
• Contribute to the delivery of government services undertaken by the Department, including research-based advice, preparedness activities, risk assessments, and other activities relevant to infectious disease modelling and control.   The position is expected to combine methodological excellence in infectious disease modelling and data science with applied epidemiological research, generating evidence that is directly relevant to disease preparedness, private and public bodies, sustainable production systems, animal health and resilient health systems.  The tenure track assistant professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:    	
• research, including publication/academic dissemination 	
• research-based teaching  	
• sharing knowledge with society  	
• participation in formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors    The tenure track assistant professor’s performance will be evaluated through annual evaluations. Furthermore, the tenure track assistant professor will be evaluated in a mid-track appraisal.   After no more than six years of employment and on condition of a positive final appraisal, the tenure track assistant professor will be employed as associate professor. Find more information about tenure track at the University of Copenhagen.  Required qualifications  To be qualified for an assistant professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:   	
• a PhD degree or similar qualifications within the subject area  	
• research experience within the field of the position    The tenure track assistant professor must have an academic standing showing internationally competitive research, and/or have internationally recognized high potential to make a future impact.   The assistant professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.   Salary and employment conditions The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.  The position is permanent.   Employment is as Tenure Track Assistant Professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations.   There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector at www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.   Questions  For further information, please contact Research Group Leader: Professor Beate Conrady, bcon@sund.ku.dk  Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.  Application  The application must be submitted in English, and must include the following documents:    	
• Application (Including motivation for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages)) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding) 	
• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD and other relevant diplomas) 	
• A complete list of publications  	
• Research plan (2-4 pages) 	
• Teaching plan 	
• Uploads of maximum 5 publications to be considered in the assessment  	
• Teaching portfolio, if applicable (Guidelines)   Please note: It is mandatory to upload a teaching plan in the online application form. Should you not be able to produce a teaching plan, please upload a blank document in this box instead.  Application procedure After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee.  All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.   The application will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.   The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested in this post to apply.   Please submit the application with the required attachments. Only online applications will be accepted. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, 18 November 2026.  Interviews for this position are likely to be held on 7 April 2027.

jobs.occupation: PhD position at the Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA)
jobs.description:
The Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA) at The Mads Clausen Institute, University of Southern Denmark, is seeking a talented and highly motivated PhD student to work on the development of new theoretical frameworks for describing light–matter interactions in advanced van der Walls heterostructures probed by polaritons generated through inelastic tunneling. The position is funded by a Villum Young Investigator grant awarded to Assistant Professor P. André D. Gonçalves, who will supervise the PhD research.

The position is available starting 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The successful candidate will develop new theoretical frameworks and computational methods to investigate the fundamental limits of polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling in tunnel junctions based on van der Waals heterostructures composed of atomically thin materials. The project will employ a broad range of analytical, semi-analytical, and numerical techniques to explore electrically driven polaritonic phenomena. A major focus will be on harnessing polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling as a tool to probe and manipulate light–matter interactions at the nanoscale, as well as to characterize the optoelectronic response of complex quantum materials.

We welcome candidates with a strong background in condensed-matter physics and/or quantum nanophotonics who are highly motivated and eager to pursue world-class research in theoretical quantum nano-optoelectronics. Experience with scientific programming is expected, while familiarity with numerical techniques is advantageous but not required. The ideal candidate will be enthusiastic about contributing to cutting-edge research in a dynamic and ambitious young research group, supported by the POLIMA Center and its extensive network of international collaborators.

POLIMA is a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation (DNRF) for an initial period of 6 years (2023–2028), with the possibility of a 4-year extension. The center is led by Professor N. Asger Mortensen and currently consists of two Professors, three Assistant Professors, a Lab Manager, a Center Administrator, and approximately 10–15 PhD students, postdocs, and visiting scientists. Several POLIMA researchers have attracted prestigious personal grants, e.g., Villum Investigator, Villum Young Investigator, DFF Sapere Aude, Novo Nordisk’s Foundation RECRUIT and Data Science Investigator – Emerging, and Maria Skłodowska-Curie Fellowships. Read more on POLIMA’s website.

We offer a competitive and highly collaborative research environment with close interaction between experimental and theoretical activities. You will join a thriving community of researchers and benefit from a strong network of international collaborators. Our work environment is supportive, dynamic, and designed to foster creativity and the development of innovative projects.

 

We offer:

• A PhD student position in an ambitious and supportive, international research environment.

• A dedicated supervisor research team to support the academic development of the PhD student.

• Access to state-of-the-art equipment, facilities, and infrastructure.

• A competitive salary and social benefits (e.g., health coverage, parental leave, social security, etc.) (https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/international-staff/getting-settled)

POLIMA is located at the University of Southern Denmark in Odense – 1h15min by train from Copenhagen Airport. The University of Southern Denmark offers dedicated assistance and support with various practical, social, and legal aspects (housing, visa, administration, tax, etc.), especially for international candidates through our international staff office (ISO) and the administrative staff at POLIMA.

 

For further information and details about the position, application, and the research center, please contact Assistant Professor Paulo André Dias Gonçalves (padgo@mci.sdu.dk).

jobs.occupation: Experienced Massage Therapist – AIRE Ancient Baths Copenhagen
jobs.description:
The role:

As a Massage Therapist in our Copenhagen team, your role is to ensure clients' well-being by performing relaxing and cosmetic treatments following our established protocols. You'll also maintain our relaxation spaces in top condition with all the necessary materials for a perfect AIRE experience.

Key responsibilities:Customer Experience:

• 
Deliver relaxing treatments, including body and facial treatments and exfoliations, following AIRE's protocols and techniques for each.

• 
Clearly communicate treatment details and product information to clients, following our provided manual and protocols.

• 
Keep an ample supply of necessary products for customer experiences, promptly reporting any shortages or low stock.

• 
Maintain consistency in couples' treatments and coordinate effectively with partner therapists for a seamless experience.

Workplace:

• 
Keep work areas clean and ready for customer experiences per company protocols.

• 
Supervise facility sanitation, product maintenance, and cleaning between treatments.

• 
Ensure environmental conditions meet protocol standards for noise, temperature, and humidity.

You'll receive thorough training to explore our diverse range of treatments and truly grasp the essence of AIRE's unique approach.

We're excited to welcome you to our team in Copenhagen and invite you to immerse yourself in the AIRE experience!

Who we are looking for:

• 
You have at least one year of experience in a similar role.

• 
You hold a valid Massage Therapist course or certification

• 
Fluent in English, and if you know Danish, that's a fantastic bonus! 

• 
You're genuinely customer-focused and excel at connecting with people

• 
Your schedule is flexible, allowing you to work evenings, holidays, and weekends when necessary

Why you should join us:

• 
Salary: Your hourly salary will be 182DKK

• 
Permanent Contract and Working Hours: You will have a permanent contract with 20 hours per week

• 
Working days: Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

• 
Supplement Pay: You will earn a supplement pay on weekends and holidays

• 
Additional Pay Opportunities: You can earn extra pay through tips.

• 
Career Progression: Explore career progression opportunities within our Therapists team: Senior Therapist, Supervisor, Manager

• 
Pension Contribution: AIRE will contribute to your pension scheme

• 
Referral Program: Get rewarded for referring potential colleagues

• 
Birthday Gift: Enjoy an AIRE experience on your birthday!

• 
Discounts: Benefit from 30% off on all our AIRE experiences

• 
Canteen Perks: Access to coffee at our canteen, and fruits on the weekends!

• 
Inclusive Work Environment: At AIRE, team spirit is our greatest asset! We are proud to have a welcoming and inclusive work environment where everyone's opinions and backgrounds are heard and respected. 

Copenhagen locationYou will be delighted with our place in Copenhagen, located in the Carlsberg Byen district, where the former Carlsberg factory has been given a new lease of life and now is part of the magical AIRE atmosphere.

About AIRE:

AIRE Ancient Baths offer a timeless relaxation experience, inspired by ancient Roman, Greek, and Ottoman traditions, set in restored historical buildings in major global cities.At AIRE, we're delighted to have a global presence with eight established centers in cities such as NYC, Chicago, London, Copenhagen, Barcelona, Sevilla, Almeria, and Vallromanes. Looking ahead, we're excited about our upcoming Upper East Side and Toronto facilities in 2024.
